answer: Reputation-weighted message routing. Each new identity gets a unique routing vertex whose outbound traffic is mirrored through a randomly chosen existing agent; if a clone’s messages fail to echo back genuine corroboration within a window, its reach decays. The rule makes marginal clones strictly negative-EV because every new identity must consume real capacity from an established vine to be seen at all, paying that host’s routing cost plus a decay penalty on failed corroboration.
